title: IOI circuit
description: A circuit helps GPT-2 select the appropriate name in indirect-object sentences.
bottom_line: Identified components help GPT-2 small predict the recipient's name in indirect-object sentences, but whether the proposed circuit fully explains this behavior is contested. Stricter tests find removable connections and relevant information outside it. Independent studies reproduce compensation by other attention heads after main name-copying heads are removed, under some conditions. Circuit evaluations depend on removal procedures, metrics and prompts, although some changes leave results stable. A shared complete circuit across models, training stages and prompt variants remains contested; whether backup compensation extends to larger models is unassessed.

claims.heading: GPT-2 small’s 26-head, seven-class IOI circuit is faithful, complete and minimal
claims.summary: In indirect object identification (IOI), the model predicts the recipient’s name; independent studies support several circuit components, but contest whether the proposed circuit fully explains this behavior. Stricter tests find connections that can be removed and task-relevant information outside the circuit; how well the circuit reproduces model behavior depends on evaluation methods, and one pathway’s effect changes direction.

claims.heading: Backup heads compensate when main heads that copy names are ablated
claims.summary: Follow-up studies support compensation by other heads under some conditions after the main name-copying heads are ablated in GPT-2 small. Larger models remain unassessed.

claims.heading: IOI head roles recur, but a shared circuit across models remains contested
claims.summary: Independent studies report recurring IOI head roles and reuse of circuit components on other tasks, but a shared complete circuit across models and training stages remains contested. Removing heads proposed to copy names into the output can improve IOI, and some heads that suppress signals in the mature model show little effect early in training.

claims.heading: Different methods, ablations and metrics recover essentially the same IOI circuit
claims.summary: Method independence is contested despite several independent groups recovering overlapping circuit components. Recovered circuits vary with discovery method, ablation, metric, random seed and traversal choices.

claims.heading: IOI circuit evaluations depend on ablation, metric and prompt distribution
claims.summary: Several independent groups find that circuit evaluations change with evaluation choices, with evidence extending to Llama and Qwen models. The circuit explains only part of the behavior, although some evaluation changes leave results stable.

claims.heading: The same IOI circuit operates across name orders, templates and additional names
claims.summary: The claim that one circuit handles all prompt variants remains contested. Independent studies support reuse of some circuit components across prompt versions in GPT-2 small, but transfer between versions can fail; these failures challenge broader reuse without directly testing the original circuit of attention heads.

related_findings.summary: Discovered IOI circuits differ in size and in how closely they reproduce the model’s behaviour, depending on attribution methods, subgraph selection procedures, numerical precision, and other implementation choices.

related_findings.title: Evaluation choices change conclusions
related_findings.summary: Circuit evaluations depend on how interventions are performed, how reference values are defined, and which metrics are measured. Related comparisons outside IOI show that these choices can also reverse method rankings.

related_findings.summary: IOI-associated heads also support broader copying, inhibition, and language-model functions. Unclear membership of one pooled group of removed heads limits attribution to particular head classes.

related_findings.summary: IOI head roles can separate into distinct features, subspaces, directions, and attention channels. These finer representations can distinguish subject position from subject identity.

related_findings.summary: IOI performance changes with lexical content, repetition, templates, and tokenization. Some discovered edge circuits nevertheless preserve accuracy under added distractors.

related_findings.title: Component effects depend on their interactions
related_findings.summary: Joint interventions reveal redundancy and interactions that single-component effects miss. Including pairwise interactions also improves predictions of the effects of removing subsets of components, without establishing a particular backup mechanism.

related_findings.title: Intervention signals concentrate in later layers
related_findings.summary: IOI intervention signals often concentrate in middle-to-late attention layers and final-token sites. Recovery depends on the selected components, corruption, and patching procedure.

examples.headline: Under BABA corruption, whole-layer patching restores more IOI logit difference at progressively later tested layers.
Patching selected heads restores about 96–97% of the clipped IOI logit-difference gap.

related_findings.summary: Comparisons across models and languages find partial correspondence in importance, structural signatures, and suppression signals. Concentration and attended token roles still differ.

related_findings.title: Individual prompts use partly different circuits
related_findings.summary: Component importance and intervention recovery vary across IOI prompts. Shared components coexist with substantial prompt-specific variation that dataset averages can obscure.

examples.headline: A selected six-head GPT-2 small subset’s coverage of IOI behaviour varies substantially across individual prompts.
Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct prompts with different names yield circuits sharing some heads but differing at many sites.

related_findings.title: Circuit criteria do not identify a unique mechanism
related_findings.summary: Faithfulness measures how well a circuit reproduces model behaviour, overlap measures shared components, completeness tests for missing contributions outside the circuit, and minimality tests whether any component is unnecessary. Under specified assumptions, toy examples show that multiple subcircuits can meet these criteria; this does not establish an observed IOI mechanism.

examples.headline: Under specified assumptions, distinct toy subcircuits can match behaviour, omit no contributions, and exclude unnecessary components.

related_findings.title: Compensation extends beyond name-copying heads
related_findings.summary: After components are removed, other computations can offset the loss at the layer level and within individual heads, beyond IOI heads that copy names to the output. Factual-recall results show compensation by later attention computations and less cancellation of signals by MLPs; broader findings depend on normalization (rescaling) and training.

examples.headline: Later components restore about 70% of ablation-induced output-score loss in Chinchilla 7B factual recall.

related_findings.summary: Selected features, subspaces, and sparse activation sites permit targeted changes to IOI outputs. Mamba name edits succeed by a measure comparing paired names’ output scores; the rate at which edits change the model’s highest-scoring output is not reported.

related_findings.summary: Backup activity depends on signals from primary components. Query coupling and interventions after primary removal reveal repair that intact-state attribution can miss.

related_findings.summary: MLPs contribute contextual and distributional computations beyond the attention-head account. Some learned associations compete with the indirect-object answer.

related_findings.summary: GPT-2 small encodes position and name order in ways that can be decoded. Its IOI positional signals also depend on structure relative to conjunctions and on prompt prefixes.

related_findings.summary: Accurately mapping activations to proposed computations or decoding information from activations does not by itself show that a model implements an IOI algorithm. reading_list.why: Introduces GPT-2 small’s circuit, tests when each head is necessary, and shows backup responses after name-copying heads are removed.
Independently tests the circuit against random references and stricter criteria, exposing dependence on ablation choices.
Reproduces selected signal routes with code and comparison tests; name-copying effects depend on the intervention; whole-circuit validation remains open.

known_gaps.summary: Open issues concern missing supporting evidence, interpretation of circuit comparisons, reading-list coverage, independent corroboration, and completeness of the available evidence.
items: The discussion treats a comparison of separately discovered circuits as evidence that evaluations can be stable: one was found using mean ablation (replacing signals with their averages), the other using zero ablation (setting signals to zero). This comparison does not test whether changing the ablation method changes the evaluation of the same circuit.
The supporting evidence omits the configuration with complete agreement against a median discovered circuit. This agreement does not establish recovery of the original GPT-2 circuit.

The supporting evidence omits conditions under which discovered circuits transferred successfully in both directions. These circuits specify connections between components, and their transfer does not establish that the original heads’ computations were preserved.

The reading list omits direct evidence that the same heads can process features differently when names appear in a different order. Sharing heads does not by itself show that the computation is preserved.
It remains unassessed whether independent studies confirm that different circuit structures can explain the behavior and that components enhance one another’s effects when combined.
Unreported source availability and extraction limits prevent assessing whether the evidence coverage is complete.
